claims: This system will take your snowmobile from approx. 145 hp to approx. 200 hp and above with higher boost levels.
Turbo system comes preset at 3-10 psi with the ability to run up to 12 psi.
With its lightweight design, the Ski-Doo 850 Turbo System adds less than 12 pounds.
The installation of the turbo system is simple and doesn't require any modification of the chassis or re-flashing of the ECU.
requirements: Base fuel mapping included. Digital fuel controller tuning required for specific machine setup for optimum functionality.

Initial tank following turbo system install: 110 race fuel or equivalent. Boost levels from 3-4lbs: 91 Octane with no more than 10% ethanol. Boost levels from 5-7lbs: Mix of 50% 91 Octane with 50% 110 race fuel or equivalent. Boost levels from 7lbs and up: 110 race fuel or equivalent.
Clutching (not included with this system).
Secondary injectors must be added and the machine tuned through the fuel controller.
mods.impact_note: This transforms the sled — and changes what owning it means. The maker claims roughly 145 hp becomes roughly 200 hp and above, but clutching is not included, secondary injectors must be added, and the machine must be tuned through the fuel controller for your specific setup. Fuel discipline is strict and set by the maker: 110 race fuel for the first tank and at boost of 7 lb and up, a 50/50 mix of 91 octane and 110 at 5–7 lb, and 91 octane only at low boost. Factory warranty is effectively gone, and engine life now depends on tune and fuel discipline.

Standard kit ships without intercooler.
No clutch kit or clutching components are listed as included.
mods.impact_note: This transforms a Gen 4 sled, but read the conditions first: the maker's page showed the kit sold out when checked. Silber's distinctive approach is a proprietary reflash of the factory ECU — your ECU must be sent in for it — after which the maker claims no further tuning is needed whatever boost or elevation you run, with boost adjustable in the 3–10 psi range. No clutch kit or clutching components are included and the standard kit ships without an intercooler, so the headline price is not the whole spend; a turbocharged engine also ends any realistic factory warranty expectation and lives or dies by boost and fuel discipline.

claims: This system will take your snowmobile from approx. 145 hp to approx. 200 hp and above with higher boost levels.
Turbo system comes preset at 3-10 psi with the ability to run up to 12 psi.
With its lightweight design, the Ski-Doo 850 Turbo System adds less than 12 pounds.

requirements: Base fuel mapping included. Digital fuel controller tuning required for specific machine setup for optimum functionality.

Initial tank following turbo system install: 110 race fuel or equivalent. Boost levels from 3-4lbs: 91 Octane with no more than 10% ethanol. Boost levels from 5-7lbs: Mix of 50% 91 Octane with 50% 110 race fuel or equivalent. Boost levels from 7lbs and up: 110 race fuel or equivalent.
Clutching (not included with this system).
Secondary injectors must be added and the machine tuned through the fuel controller.
mods.impact_note: This transforms the sled — and changes what owning it means. The maker claims roughly 145 hp becomes roughly 200 hp and above, but clutching is not included, secondary injectors must be added, and the machine must be tuned through the fuel controller for your specific setup. Fuel discipline is strict and set by the maker: 110 race fuel for the first tank and at boost of 7 lb and up, a 50/50 mix of 91 octane and 110 at 5–7 lb, and 91 octane only at low boost. Factory warranty is effectively gone, and engine life now depends on tune and fuel discipline.

mods.impact_note: This transforms a Gen 4 sled, but read the conditions first: the maker's page showed the kit sold out when checked. Silber's distinctive approach is a proprietary reflash of the factory ECU — your ECU must be sent in for it — after which the maker claims no further tuning is needed whatever boost or elevation you run, with boost adjustable in the 3–10 psi range. No clutch kit or clutching components are included and the standard kit ships without an intercooler, so the headline price is not the whole spend; a turbocharged engine also ends any realistic factory warranty expectation and lives or dies by boost and fuel discipline.

mods.product_name: Lynx / Ski-Doo 850 Turbo System — Ski-Doo Gen 4 (2017-2022) variant
mods.fitment_statement: Maker fitment list (records follow the named list, not the headline 'all Ski-Doo 850 & Lynx naturally aspirated units'): Backcountry / Backcountry X / Backcountry X-RS 850 (2019-2024), Freeride 850 Naturally Aspirated (2018-2024), Summit 850 Naturally Aspirated (2017-2024), Summit X 850 Naturally Aspirated (2017-2024), Summit Edge 850 (2022-2023), Summit SP 850 (2023); Lynx Boondocker DS 3900 / DS 4100 (2022), Shredder DS 3900 Naturally Aspirated (2023-2024), Shredder RE Naturally Aspirated (2023), Shredder RE 3700 / 3900 Naturally Aspirated (2024). No MXZ, Renegade or Expedition entries are printed. No maker-stated coverage for 2025-2026.
claims: This system will take your snowmobile from approx. 145 hp to approx. 200 hp and above with higher boost levels.
Turbo system comes preset at 3-10 psi with the ability to run up to 12 psi.
With its lightweight design, the Ski-Doo 850 Turbo System adds less than 12 pounds.
The installation of the turbo system is simple and doesn't require any modification of the chassis or re-flashing of the ECU.
requirements: Base fuel mapping included. Digital fuel controller tuning required for specific machine setup for optimum functionality.

Initial tank following turbo system install: 110 race fuel or equivalent. Boost levels from 3-4lbs: 91 Octane with no more than 10% ethanol. Boost levels from 5-7lbs: Mix of 50% 91 Octane with 50% 110 race fuel or equivalent. Boost levels from 7lbs and up: 110 race fuel or equivalent.
Clutching (not included with this system).
Secondary injectors must be added and the machine tuned through the fuel controller.
mods.impact_note: This transforms the sled — and changes what owning it means. The maker claims roughly 145 hp becomes roughly 200 hp and above, but clutching is not included, secondary injectors must be added, and the machine must be tuned through the fuel controller for your specific setup. Fuel discipline is strict and set by the maker: 110 race fuel for the first tank and at boost of 7 lb and up, a 50/50 mix of 91 octane and 110 at 5–7 lb, and 91 octane only at low boost. Factory warranty is effectively gone, and engine life now depends on tune and fuel discipline.

mods.product_name: Ski-Doo (Lynx) G4 850 Turbo Kit 2017-2022
mods.fitment_statement: Product title (maker-stated at generation + years level; no individual models named): Ski-Doo (Lynx) G4 850 Turbo Kit 2017-2022. Maker lists the kit from $3,250.00 USD depending on variant; headline price $3,750.00 USD. Shown as Sold out on the maker page at check date.
claims: We are the first company to utilize the factory ECU/ECM to control fueling requirements for the turbo. This means no tuning no matter what boost you run or what elevation you run at.
Boost levels adjustable by the user between 3-10psi; with wastegate actuator springs, control your boost from 3-12psi. Silber notes the kit comes preset with a 7psi spring.
This kit is the easiest turbo to install on the market with no cutting, welding or drilling required.
requirements: ECU must be sent in for Silber's proprietary reflash: "Do I need to send back my ECU for a reflash? Yes you need to send us your ECU if you purchase a kit."
Standard kit ships without intercooler.
No clutch kit or clutching components are listed as included.
mods.impact_note: This transforms a Gen 4 sled, but read the conditions first: the maker's page showed the kit sold out when checked. Silber's distinctive approach is a proprietary reflash of the factory ECU — your ECU must be sent in for it — after which the maker claims no further tuning is needed whatever boost or elevation you run, with boost adjustable in the 3–10 psi range. No clutch kit or clutching components are included and the standard kit ships without an intercooler, so the headline price is not the whole spend; a turbocharged engine also ends any realistic factory warranty expectation and lives or dies by boost and fuel discipline.

not_listed.reason: Dalton's own FAQ states it does not offer application-specific clutch kits or fitment guides, so there is no maker-stated fitment for this sled.

mods.product_name: Ski-Doo Etec 850 N.A Stage 2 Clutch Kit
mods.fitment_statement: These kits are matched to platform and engine configuration — N.A. Etec 850, Gen 4 Factory Turbo, or Gen 5 Factory Turbo — rather than a specific model year. The N.A. Stage 2 kit is built for the standard, non-turbo Etec 850.
claims: Faster Backshifting
Increased Top-End Track Speed
Improved Throttle Response
Each weight provides 20g of adjustability, thanks to the included .85g and 1.7g magnets.
mods.impact_note: Adds no power — it changes how the power you have reaches the snow, and the maker claims faster backshifting, increased top-end track speed and improved throttle response. The gain shows up in deep snow and on climbs, where quick backshifting keeps track speed up under load, and the magnetic weights let you fine-tune without a full teardown. It is bolt-in and reversible, though a clutch puller and spring compressor make the job easier — and the maker's page showed it sold out when checked.

mods.product_name: Performance Big Bore Ultimate Kit / Skidoo 911
mods.fitment_statement: 911 big bore top end kit fits all 2017+ 850 E-TEC models
claims: 190hp on pump gas fuel and 200 hp on 110 octane fuel
Huge mid-range and torque gain!
Complete kit with everything you need to go from 850 to 911.
requirements: Must send in cylinders, exhaust valves (blades only), and head unless you select to purchase outright.
Exchange (core send-in) price: $3,795.95 USD.
mods.impact_note: This is a system, not a bolt-on — cylinders, pistons, pipe, y-pipe, fuel module and a Stage 2 clutch kit are all in the box, because a bigger engine on stock exhaust and clutching would waste the displacement. The maker claims 190 hp on pump gas and 200 hp on 110 octane; the second figure comes with a race-fuel routine, and both are maker claims, not verified numbers. Unless you buy outright you must send in your cylinders, exhaust valves and head, so the sled is down while that happens, and a modified engine like this ends any realistic expectation of factory engine warranty coverage.

mods.product_name: '17-22 E-TEC 850 FULL VELOCITY MUFFLER - BLACK
mods.fitment_statement: Fitment stated in the product name: 2017-2022 E-TEC 850 (Gen4).
claims: Proven performance that works!!
All mufflers are extensively tested on our Superflow 902 dyno to ensure the best performance.
mods.impact_note: This is a weight-and-sound mod, not a proven power mod: Bikeman says its mufflers are extensively dyno-tested to ensure the best performance, but prints no weight or power figure for this version. Expect a louder, freer-flowing can and whatever front-end weight comes off with the stock muffler, with noise the main thing other riders will notice. Some trail systems and jurisdictions restrict aftermarket mufflers, so it suits mountain and off-trail use better than noise-sensitive trails.

mods.product_name: Powder Lite Muffler for Ski-Doo 850 E-Tec (2017-2022) - Black
mods.fitment_statement: Fitment stated in the product name: 2017-2022 E-TEC 850 (Gen4).
claims: Weighing in at a mere 5 lbs, the Powder Lite sheds a massive 10 lbs of unwanted factory weight right off the front end.
mods.impact_note: The maker claims this muffler weighs a mere 5 lb and sheds 10 lb of factory weight off the front end — as with most cans, that weight saving and a much louder note are the real purchase, not a verified power gain. It is a race/mountain-style can, so it will be substantially louder than stock and a poor fit where trail muffler rules are enforced. It suits mountain riders chasing front-end weight savings who ride away from noise enforcement.

mods.product_name: '17-22 E-TEC 850 POWDER LITE MUFFLER - CERAMIC

Loses 10 lbs of unwanted weight from your sled

Compatible models list names Summit, Freeride, MXZ, Renegade, Backcountry and Expedition / Skandic 850 E-TEC.
claims: Dyno-Proven Gain: +4–5 Peak HP & Stronger Sustained Top-End Pull (SuperFlow 902 Dyno Verified)
delivering a proven 4 to 5 horsepower gain and noticeably stronger torque across the entire RPM range
requirements: Bolt-On Compatible (No ECU tune required for standalone installation)

mods.product_name: 2017-20 850 Ski-Doo G4 Summit Single Pipe Set – PicNic'R Style
mods.fitment_statement: For 2017-20 Ski-Doo 850 Summit, Freeride and 2017 Renegade Backcountry/Backcountry X
claims: Boost horsepower (+7.3 horsepower) and performance while bringing out your inner chef.

Trail Chef Cooker (Part #46-107) not included.
mods.impact_note: This is a full single pipe set, not just a can, and the maker claims +7.3 horsepower and 9.9 lb saved — a matched pipe is where a naturally aspirated gain is most plausible, but it remains a maker claim. SLP says some clutching changes are recommended and no ECU modification is required, and says the set passed the SAE J-2567 stationary sound test below 88 decibels. The PicNic'R twist is a built-in cooker mount on the silencer — and the Trail Chef Cooker itself is not included, so budget for it if that is the attraction.

claims: This system will take your snowmobile from approx. 145 hp to approx. 200 hp and above with higher boost levels.

Secondary injectors must be added and the machine tuned through the fuel controller.
mods.impact_note: This transforms the sled — and changes what owning it means. The maker claims roughly 145 hp becomes roughly 200 hp and above, but clutching is not included, secondary injectors must be added, and the machine must be tuned through the fuel controller for your specific setup. Fuel discipline is strict and set by the maker: 110 race fuel for the first tank and at boost of 7 lb and up, a 50/50 mix of 91 octane and 110 at 5–7 lb, and 91 octane only at low boost. Factory warranty is effectively gone, and engine life now depends on tune and fuel discipline.

No clutch kit or clutching components are included and the standard kit ships without an intercooler, so the headline price is not the whole spend; a turbocharged engine also ends any realistic factory warranty expectation and lives or dies by boost and fuel discipline.

claims: Boost horsepower (+7.3 horsepower) and performance while bringing out your inner chef.
This kit also reduces weight by 9.9 pounds.
SLP tested and passed SAE J-2567 stationary sound test below 88 decibels.
requirements: Some clutching changes recommended see instruction sheet for more info.
No ECU modification required.
Trail Chef Cooker (Part #46-107) not included.
mods.impact_note: This is a full single pipe set, not just a can, and the maker claims +7.3 horsepower and 9.9 lb saved — a matched pipe is where a naturally aspirated gain is most plausible, but it remains a maker claim. SLP says some clutching changes are recommended and no ECU modification is required, and says the set passed the SAE J-2567 stationary sound test below 88 decibels. The PicNic'R twist is a built-in cooker mount on the silencer — and the Trail Chef Cooker itself is not included, so budget for it if that is the attraction.

mods.product_name: Comp. Series Silencer for Ski-Doo 850 G4/G5 Models
mods.fitment_statement: Variant options captured on the maker page: 2017-20 850 G4 (Part #09-326), 2021-22 850 G4 (Part #09-342). No G5 variant was captured; not extended to Gen5.
claims: It provides up to 9.1 pounds of weight savings.
It passes the stationary sound test below 88 decibels but gives a more exciting sound at the higher RPM ranges.
mods.impact_note: Built with the competition racer in mind: the maker claims up to 9.1 lb saved, says it passes the stationary sound test below 88 decibels, and is open that it runs several decibels louder than its quiet silencer at wide-open throttle, with slightly improved throttle response. That makes it a weight-first can for riders who accept more noise at full throttle. The fitment variants captured from the maker are Gen 4 only, despite the G4/G5 product title, so Gen 5 riders should not assume coverage.

mods.product_name: Ski-Doo 850 REV Gen 4, Gen 5 & Lynx Radian High-Performance Y-Pipe
mods.fitment_statement: Product title: Ski-Doo 850 REV Gen 4, Gen 5 & Lynx Radian High-Performance Y-Pipe (ceramic coated 134-174; high-temp black 134-175 per the maker instruction sheets). Price range by coating option: $249.95 to $274.95 USD.
claims: The Straightline Performance High-Performance Y-Pipe for Ski-Doo REV Gen 4, Gen 5, and Lynx 850 models delivers a proven 5+ horsepower gain
There are no fuel programming changes required to run the Straightline 850 E-TEC Ypipe.
requirements: Straightline recommends adding an Adjustable P-Drive Weights to your snowmobile to help enhance the power.
mods.impact_note: A y-pipe is a supporting piece, not a full exhaust: the maker claims a proven 5+ horsepower gain, which is a maker claim, and says no fuel programming changes are required to run it. Straightline recommends adding adjustable pDrive weights to help enhance the power, which is an honest signal that clutching may be needed to use whatever gain is there. On its own the change is modest — it makes most sense as part of a matched exhaust package.

mods.product_name: 2017-24 Ski-doo Rev Gen 4 & 5 / Lynx Raiden 850 E-TEC Summit 146-175″ Track 6000ft+ Clutch Kit
mods.fitment_statement: 2017-23 Ski-doo/Lynx Rev Gen 4&5 850 E-TEC Summit/ Freeride 146-175″ Track 6000ft Clutch Kit; maker fitment table also lists Ski-Doo Backcountry and Lynx (RAIDEN) rows, 2017–2024 (part #121-240 per the maker Y-pipe instruction sheet).
claims: High Elevation Off-trail Clutch Kit for the Ski-Doo 850 designed for 146-175″ tracks improves Acceleration, track speed, and back shift
requirements: Elevation-specific: 6000ft+ calibration.
mods.impact_note: This kit adds no power — it is a high-elevation calibration for long-track mountain sleds, and the maker claims it improves acceleration, track speed and backshift. That calibration is specific to 6000 ft and above and to 146–175-inch tracks, so it will be the wrong kit at low elevation or on a short track. It suits high-altitude Summit and Freeride riders whose stock clutching feels lazy in thin air and deep snow.

mods.product_name: GGB Mountain Muffler — Ski-Doo Gen 4 850 E-TEC
mods.fitment_statement: GGB's per-year/per-model fitment list for this part number (ggbexhaust.com, checked 2026-11-21), summarised by the maker's own short-form list: 2017-2022 Gen 4 850 E-TEC MXZ/Renegade/Summit/Backcountry/Freeride, plus 2023 Gen 4 Backcountry / Backcountry X / Backcountry XRS; the same list names Lynx Boondocker DS, Rave RE and Xterrain RE entries for 2022–2023 (full list in research notes). No Expedition 850 entry appears in the list.
claims: Stock Muffler: 15.75  GGB Mountain: 5.1  Weight Savings: 10.65 lbs
Guaranteed to provide performance levels as good as or better than stock
Sound level increase over stock (dbA) Idle + 4-6 / Under load + 10-18
requirements: Fuel and clutching mods are not necessary prior to installation.
mods.impact_note: This is a weight-and-sound mod, not a power mod: the maker claims 10.65 lb saved and prints the noise honestly, +4–6 dBA at idle and +10–18 dBA under load. No fuel or clutching changes are needed, so install is simple, but that under-load noise makes it a backcountry part, not a trail part — some trail systems and jurisdictions restrict aftermarket mufflers. The maker's page showed this Gen 4 version currently out of stock when checked.

mods.product_name: GGB Trail Muffler — Ski-Doo Gen 4 850 E-TEC
mods.fitment_statement: GGB's per-year/per-model fitment list for this part number (ggbexhaust.com, checked 2026-11-21), summarised by the maker's own short-form list: 2017-2022 Gen 4 850 E-TEC MXZ/Renegade/Summit/Backcountry/Freeride, plus 2023 Gen 4 Backcountry / Backcountry X / Backcountry XRS; the same list names Lynx Boondocker DS, Rave RE and Xterrain RE entries for 2022–2023 (full list in research notes). No Expedition 850 entry appears in the list.
claims: Stock Muffler: 15.75  GGB Trail: 7.7  Weight Savings: 8.05 lbs
System fits securely in the original location using stock mounts and is guaranteed to provide performance levels as good as or better than stock.
Sound level increase over stock: (dbA) Idle + 3-6 / Under load + 3-6
requirements: Fuel and clutching mods are not necessary prior to installation.
mods.impact_note: GGB positions the Trail as the populated-area option: the maker claims 8.05 lb saved and a much smaller sound increase than the Mountain, +3–6 dBA at idle and under load, and says it is designed for use where sound levels are strictly enforced. No fuel or clutching changes are needed, and the maker guarantees performance as good as or better than stock — a maker claim, as with every can here. It is the GGB most defensible on a trail sled, though local muffler rules can still apply.

mods.product_name: GGB Quiet Muffler — Ski-Doo Gen 4 850 E-TEC
mods.fitment_statement: GGB's per-year/per-model fitment list for this part number (ggbexhaust.com, checked 2026-11-21), summarised by the maker's own short-form list: 2017-2022 Gen 4 850 E-TEC MXZ/Renegade/Summit/Backcountry/Freeride, plus 2023 Gen 4 Backcountry / Backcountry X / Backcountry XRS; the same list names Lynx Boondocker DS, Rave RE and Xterrain RE entries for 2022–2023 (full list in research notes). No Expedition 850 entry appears in the list.
claims: Stock Muffler: 15.75  GGB Quiet: 9.0  Weight Savings: 6.75 lbs
Dyno tested to provide as good as or better than stock performance.
requirements: Fuel and clutching mods are not necessary prior to installation.
mods.impact_note: The Quiet is the restrained end of GGB's range: the maker claims 6.75 lb saved and dyno-tested performance as good as or better than stock, for riders who want a deeper note and the weight saving without the Mountain muffler's noise penalty. No fuel or clutching changes are needed. It is still an aftermarket muffler where muffler rules are enforced — and the maker's page showed this Gen 4 version currently out of stock when checked.

mods.product_name: Race Series Snowmobile Exhaust, 1320309
mods.fitment_statement: Upgrade your 2017-2023 Ski-Doo GEN 4 Chassis 850 E-TEC | 2022-2022 Lynx BOONDOCKER DS | 2022-2023 Lynx RAVE RE with the MBRP Exhaust. Vehicle Configuration: Does Not Fit Wide-Body Models (Excludes - Expedition, Grand Touring, Enduro, Skandic).

Race — Maximum weight savings, high-flow design, serious sound.
T304 Stainless Steel
2-Year Warranty
requirements: Does Not Fit Wide-Body Models (Excludes - Expedition, Grand Touring, Enduro, Skandic)
mods.impact_note: MBRP's Race series is its loud, aggressive end: the maker describes maximum weight savings, a high-flow design and serious sound, but prints no numeric power, weight or noise figure, so none can be quoted for it. In practice this is a sound-first can for riders who accept the noise — the wrong pick for groomed trails, populated areas or anywhere mufflers are checked. It does not fit wide-body models: Expedition, Grand Touring, Enduro and Skandic are excluded.

mods.product_name: Trail Series Snowmobile Exhaust, 132T207
mods.fitment_statement: Upgrade your 2017-2023 Ski-Doo GEN 4 Chassis 850 E-TEC | 2022-2022 Lynx BOONDOCKER DS | 2022-2023 Lynx RAVE RE with the MBRP Exhaust. Vehicle Configuration: Does Not Fit Wide-Body Models (Excludes - Expedition, Grand Touring, Enduro, Skandic).

requirements: Does Not Fit Wide-Body Models (Excludes - Expedition, Grand Touring, Enduro, Skandic)
mods.impact_note: MBRP's Trail series sits in the middle: the maker describes it as lightweight with a subtle tone for noise-sensitive areas, and prints no numeric power or weight figure, so the honest expectation is a modest sound change and stainless build quality (2-year warranty), not a performance gain. That makes it a reasonable trail choice where a can is allowed at all. It does not fit wide-body models: Expedition, Grand Touring, Enduro and Skandic are excluded.

mods.product_name: Quiet Series Snowmobile Exhaust, 132Q106
mods.fitment_statement: Upgrade your 2017-2023 Ski-Doo GEN 4 Chassis 850 E-TEC with the MBRP Quiet Exhaust. Vehicle Configuration: Does Not Fit Wide-Body Models (Excludes - Expedition, Grand Touring, Enduro, Skandic). (No Lynx line is printed for this part number.)

T304 Stainless Steel
2-Year Warranty
requirements: Does Not Fit Wide-Body Models (Excludes - Expedition, Grand Touring, Enduro, Skandic)
mods.impact_note: MBRP's Quiet series is the mild end of its range — the maker describes a richer exhaust note while keeping noise levels minimal, and prints no power or weight figure at all, so treat this as a sound-and-build mod (T304 stainless, 2-year warranty) rather than a performance buy. That restraint makes it the MBRP most defensible on noise-sensitive trails, though aftermarket-muffler rules can still apply. It does not fit wide-body models: Expedition, Grand Touring, Enduro and Skandic are excluded.

mods.product_name: Lynx / Ski-Doo 850 Turbo System — Ski-Doo Gen 4 (2017-2022) variant
mods.fitment_statement: Maker fitment list (records follow the named list, not the headline 'all Ski-Doo 850 & Lynx naturally aspirated units'): Backcountry / Backcountry X / Backcountry X-RS 850 (2019-2024), Freeride 850 Naturally Aspirated (2018-2024), Summit 850 Naturally Aspirated (2017-2024), Summit X 850 Naturally Aspirated (2017-2024), Summit Edge 850 (2022-2023), Summit SP 850 (2023); Lynx Boondocker DS 3900 / DS 4100 (2022), Shredder DS 3900 Naturally Aspirated (2023-2024), Shredder RE Naturally Aspirated (2023), Shredder RE 3700 / 3900 Naturally Aspirated (2024). No MXZ, Renegade or Expedition entries are printed. No maker-stated coverage for 2025-2026.
claims: This system will take your snowmobile from approx. 145 hp to approx. 200 hp and above with higher boost levels.
Turbo system comes preset at 3-10 psi with the ability to run up to 12 psi.
With its lightweight design, the Ski-Doo 850 Turbo System adds less than 12 pounds.
The installation of the turbo system is simple and doesn't require any modification of the chassis or re-flashing of the ECU.
requirements: Base fuel mapping included. Digital fuel controller tuning required for specific machine setup for optimum functionality.

Initial tank following turbo system install: 110 race fuel or equivalent. Boost levels from 3-4lbs: 91 Octane with no more than 10% ethanol. Boost levels from 5-7lbs: Mix of 50% 91 Octane with 50% 110 race fuel or equivalent. Boost levels from 7lbs and up: 110 race fuel or equivalent.
Clutching (not included with this system).
Secondary injectors must be added and the machine tuned through the fuel controller.
mods.impact_note: This transforms the sled — and changes what owning it means. The maker claims roughly 145 hp becomes roughly 200 hp and above, but clutching is not included, secondary injectors must be added, and the machine must be tuned through the fuel controller for your specific setup. Fuel discipline is strict and set by the maker: 110 race fuel for the first tank and at boost of 7 lb and up, a 50/50 mix of 91 octane and 110 at 5–7 lb, and 91 octane only at low boost. Factory warranty is effectively gone, and engine life now depends on tune and fuel discipline.

mods.product_name: Ski-Doo (Lynx) G4 850 Turbo Kit 2017-2022
mods.fitment_statement: Product title (maker-stated at generation + years level; no individual models named): Ski-Doo (Lynx) G4 850 Turbo Kit 2017-2022. Maker lists the kit from $3,250.00 USD depending on variant; headline price $3,750.00 USD. Shown as Sold out on the maker page at check date.
claims: We are the first company to utilize the factory ECU/ECM to control fueling requirements for the turbo. This means no tuning no matter what boost you run or what elevation you run at.
Boost levels adjustable by the user between 3-10psi; with wastegate actuator springs, control your boost from 3-12psi. Silber notes the kit comes preset with a 7psi spring.
This kit is the easiest turbo to install on the market with no cutting, welding or drilling required.
requirements: ECU must be sent in for Silber's proprietary reflash: "Do I need to send back my ECU for a reflash? Yes you need to send us your ECU if you purchase a kit."
Standard kit ships without intercooler.
No clutch kit or clutching components are listed as included.
mods.impact_note: This transforms a Gen 4 sled, but read the conditions first: the maker's page showed the kit sold out when checked. Silber's distinctive approach is a proprietary reflash of the factory ECU — your ECU must be sent in for it — after which the maker claims no further tuning is needed whatever boost or elevation you run, with boost adjustable in the 3–10 psi range. No clutch kit or clutching components are included and the standard kit ships without an intercooler, so the headline price is not the whole spend; a turbocharged engine also ends any realistic factory warranty expectation and lives or dies by boost and fuel discipline.

not_listed.reason: Dalton's own FAQ states it does not offer application-specific clutch kits or fitment guides, so there is no maker-stated fitment for this sled.

mods.product_name: Ski-Doo Etec 850 N.A Stage 2 Clutch Kit
mods.fitment_statement: These kits are matched to platform and engine configuration — N.A. Etec 850, Gen 4 Factory Turbo, or Gen 5 Factory Turbo — rather than a specific model year. The N.A. Stage 2 kit is built for the standard, non-turbo Etec 850.
claims: Faster Backshifting
Increased Top-End Track Speed
Improved Throttle Response
Each weight provides 20g of adjustability, thanks to the included .85g and 1.7g magnets.
mods.impact_note: Adds no power — it changes how the power you have reaches the snow, and the maker claims faster backshifting, increased top-end track speed and improved throttle response. The gain shows up in deep snow and on climbs, where quick backshifting keeps track speed up under load, and the magnetic weights let you fine-tune without a full teardown. It is bolt-in and reversible, though a clutch puller and spring compressor make the job easier — and the maker's page showed it sold out when checked.

mods.product_name: Performance Big Bore Ultimate Kit / Skidoo 911
mods.fitment_statement: 911 big bore top end kit fits all 2017+ 850 E-TEC models
claims: 190hp on pump gas fuel and 200 hp on 110 octane fuel
Huge mid-range and torque gain!
Complete kit with everything you need to go from 850 to 911.
requirements: Must send in cylinders, exhaust valves (blades only), and head unless you select to purchase outright.
Exchange (core send-in) price: $3,795.95 USD.
mods.impact_note: This is a system, not a bolt-on — cylinders, pistons, pipe, y-pipe, fuel module and a Stage 2 clutch kit are all in the box, because a bigger engine on stock exhaust and clutching would waste the displacement. The maker claims 190 hp on pump gas and 200 hp on 110 octane; the second figure comes with a race-fuel routine, and both are maker claims, not verified numbers. Unless you buy outright you must send in your cylinders, exhaust valves and head, so the sled is down while that happens, and a modified engine like this ends any realistic expectation of factory engine warranty coverage.

mods.product_name: '17-22 E-TEC 850 FULL VELOCITY MUFFLER - BLACK
mods.fitment_statement: Fitment stated in the product name: 2017-2022 E-TEC 850 (Gen4).
claims: Proven performance that works!!
All mufflers are extensively tested on our Superflow 902 dyno to ensure the best performance.
mods.impact_note: This is a weight-and-sound mod, not a proven power mod: Bikeman says its mufflers are extensively dyno-tested to ensure the best performance, but prints no weight or power figure for this version. Expect a louder, freer-flowing can and whatever front-end weight comes off with the stock muffler, with noise the main thing other riders will notice. Some trail systems and jurisdictions restrict aftermarket mufflers, so it suits mountain and off-trail use better than noise-sensitive trails.

mods.product_name: Powder Lite Muffler for Ski-Doo 850 E-Tec (2017-2022) - Black
mods.fitment_statement: Fitment stated in the product name: 2017-2022 E-TEC 850 (Gen4).
claims: Weighing in at a mere 5 lbs, the Powder Lite sheds a massive 10 lbs of unwanted factory weight right off the front end.
mods.impact_note: The maker claims this muffler weighs a mere 5 lb and sheds 10 lb of factory weight off the front end — as with most cans, that weight saving and a much louder note are the real purchase, not a verified power gain. It is a race/mountain-style can, so it will be substantially louder than stock and a poor fit where trail muffler rules are enforced. It suits mountain riders chasing front-end weight savings who ride away from noise enforcement.

mods.product_name: '17-22 E-TEC 850 POWDER LITE MUFFLER - CERAMIC
mods.fitment_statement: Fitment stated in the product name: 2017-2022 E-TEC 850 (Gen4).
claims: Only weighs 5 lbs
Loses 10 lbs of unwanted weight from your sled
The best sounding race/mountain exhaust on the market!
mods.impact_note: The maker claims this can weighs only 5 lb and loses 10 lb from the sled, and bills it as a race/mountain exhaust — weight and sound are what you are actually buying, not a verified power gain. Powder Lite cans are the loud end of the range, so the real cost is noise and exposure where mufflers are checked or trails are shared. It suits riders cutting front-end weight for mountain riding, not riders on groomed trails near homes.

mods.product_name: Performance Exhaust Manifold (Y-Pipe) for Ski-Doo 2017+ 850 E-TEC & Turbo (REV Gen4 & Gen5)
mods.fitment_statement: Engineered as a direct bolt-on upgrade for all 2017+ Ski-Doo REV Gen4 and REV Gen5 850 E-TEC snowmobiles — fitting both Naturally Aspirated (NA) and factory 850 Turbo / Turbo R models. Compatible models list names Summit, Freeride, MXZ, Renegade, Backcountry and Expedition / Skandic 850 E-TEC.
claims: Dyno-Proven Gain: +4–5 Peak HP & Stronger Sustained Top-End Pull (SuperFlow 902 Dyno Verified)
delivering a proven 4 to 5 horsepower gain and noticeably stronger torque across the entire RPM range
requirements: Bolt-On Compatible (No ECU tune required for standalone installation)
mods.impact_note: A y-pipe is a supporting piece, not a full exhaust: the maker claims a 4–5 peak horsepower gain on its dyno, which is a maker claim, and any real gain depends on the pipe and silencer downstream of it. Bikeman says no ECU tune is required to run it standalone, which makes it a low-commitment bolt-on. On its own the change is modest — it makes most sense as part of a matched exhaust package rather than as a standalone power buy.

mods.product_name: pDrive Adjustable Weight Pivot Bolt Kit (12–20.6g) for Ski-Doo 850 E-TEC
mods.fitment_statement: Primary Application: 2017+ Ski-Doo REV Gen4 & Gen5 850 E-TEC snowmobiles (Summit, Freeride, Renegade, MXZ, and Backcountry models).
claims: Adjustment Range: 12.0 grams (lighter than stock for extreme elevation) up to 20.6 grams
No Ramp or Clutch Removal: Adjust pivot mass directly on the sled in minutes using standard hand tools.
requirements: Clean internal threads before installation. Apply low-to-medium strength threadlocker to pivot bolt threads and torque to factory pDrive specifications.
mods.impact_note: This is not a full clutch kit and it adds no power — it is a set of adjustable pivot bolts that let you change primary clutch weight across the maker's stated 12–20.6 g range, which Bikeman says can be done on the sled in minutes without removing the ramps or clutch. That makes it a tuning tool for riders who change elevation or have added power elsewhere and need to correct rpm, not a performance gain by itself. Installation needs clean threads, threadlocker and torque to factory pDrive specifications, so it rewards careful work.

mods.product_name: Ski-Doo 850 Stage 1
mods.fitment_statement: Product options: 2017-18 / 2019-20 / 2021-22 / 2023-27 850 MXZ, 850 Renegade and 850 Summit (model options verbatim in research notes).
claims: This Stage 1 kit gives you 7.1 pounds of weight savings, a crisp sound with a couple extra horsepower.
requirements: Elevation calibration must be selected at order: 0-3000' or 3000'+.
mods.impact_note: Stage 1 is the lighter step: a silencer and Powder Valve intake kit, with a Power Shift clutch kit included on some models, and the maker claims 7.1 lb saved and 'a couple extra horsepower' — a deliberately modest claim. You must pick the right elevation calibration at order, 0–3000' or 3000'+, because that calibration is part of the kit. It suits riders who want weight off and a crisper sound without committing to a full pipe set.

mods.product_name: Ski-Doo 850 G4/G5: Stage 2
mods.fitment_statement: Product options: 2017-18 / 2019-20 / 2021-22 / 2023-27 850 MXZ, 850 Renegade and 850 Summit (model options verbatim in research notes).
claims: Delivering an additional 7.3 horsepower and 4.9 ft/lbs of torque while trimming 10.1 pounds of weight
An arm stretching 6 lengths quicker than stock in a 1/4 mile drag race is what you will see in the field.
requirements: Elevation calibration must be selected at order: 0-3000' or 3000'+.
Kit includes a Single Pipe Set (y-pipe, pipe and silencer), Powder Valve Intake Kit and a Power Shift Clutch Kit.
mods.impact_note: The classic naturally aspirated recipe — a matched single pipe set, intake and clutch kit tuned to work together, which is why the maker's claim is modest and specific: an additional 7.3 horsepower and 4.9 ft-lb of torque while trimming 10.1 lb. The elevation choice at order is not a formality: you must select the 0–3000' or 3000'+ calibration, and picking the wrong one gives back much of the gain. It suits riders who want a complete, matched package instead of piecing exhaust and clutching together themselves.

mods.product_name: 2017-27 850 Ski-Doo Single Pipe Sets
mods.fitment_statement: Product options: 850 Summit G4 REV, 850 MXZ and Renegade G4 REV (except 2017 Renegade Backcountry), 850 MXZ and Renegade G5, 850 Summit G5 naturally aspirated
claims: Increased horsepower and lighter weight; two things SLP exhaust systems are well known for.
mods.impact_note: This is a full pipe set, the part of the exhaust where a naturally aspirated engine can actually gain — but SLP prints no numeric power or weight figure for it, only a general claim of increased horsepower and lighter weight, so there is no number to hold it to. The kits include detailed instructions covering clutching and EFI mapping information, which tells you setup matters if you want whatever gain is there. The G4 trail fitment expressly excludes the 2017 Renegade Backcountry, so check the exact variant for your sled.

mods.product_name: 2017-27 850 Ski-Doo G4 & G5 REV Lightweight Silencer
mods.fitment_statement: Product options: 850 Summit G4 REV, 850 MXZ and Renegade G4 REV (except 2017 Renegade Backcountry), 850 MXZ and Renegade G5, 850 Summit G5 naturally aspirated
claims: These silencers reduce weight by 7.1 lbs.
SLP tested and passed SAE J-2567 stationary sound test below 88 decibels.
requirements: No ECU Modification is required.
mods.impact_note: A silencer-only mod: the maker claims 7.1 lb saved, claims no horsepower gain, and says it passed the SAE J-2567 stationary sound test below 88 decibels. No ECU modification is required, and SLP notes it is compatible with its single pipe, so a pipe can be added later. In the real world this is weight off the sled and a different note, not a power increase — the sensible buy if you may build toward a pipe later.

mods.fitment_statement: Variant options captured on the maker page: 2017-20 850 G4 (Part #09-326), 2021-22 850 G4 (Part #09-342). No G5 variant was captured; not extended to Gen5.

That makes it a weight-first can for riders who accept more noise at full throttle. mods.product_name: Clutch Kits - Ski-Doo (Power Shift Clutch Kits)
mods.fitment_statement: Product options: 850 E-TEC 2017-21 MXZ, 850 E-TEC 2017-27 Renegade, 850 E-TEC 2017-27 Summit
claims: Get your horsepower to the ground with SLP Power Shift Clutch Kits!
On short track models, these kits deliver instantaneous throttle response with wicked acceleration.
requirements: Buyer must select model, exhaust configuration (Stock/Silencer, Stock/Stage 1, Stage 1, SLP Single Pipe, Stage 2, Stage 3) and elevation band. Price shown is the maker page starting price for the multi-application page; 850 variant prices are not separated on the page.
mods.impact_note: This adds no power — it is about getting the power you have to the snow, and SLP claims its Magnum Force weights improve belt pinch, acceleration and belt slippage. You must order it matched to your model, your exhaust configuration and your elevation band; a kit ordered for the wrong exhaust or elevation misses the point entirely. Note the price carried in this data is the maker page's starting price for a multi-application page, not a separated 850 price, so confirm the actual variant price before relying on it.

mods.product_name: Skidoo 850 Rev Gen 4 / Lynx Radien High Performance Exhaust – Combo Ceramic Coated (Includes 134-173, 134-174)
mods.fitment_statement: Maker fitment table: Ski-Doo 850 E-TEC Backcountry, MXZ, Renegade, Summit for 2017–2022 plus 2023 Backcountry rows, and Lynx 850 E-TEC (RAIDEN) rows. Does not include a single pipe. (Maker table also prints 2025–2026 rows; not applied — the product is the maker-named Rev Gen 4 combo. See research notes.)
claims: HP Gain | 5 HP
Weight loss | 7.5 lbs
A Complete Performance Exhaust package at a fraction of the price, use your stock single pipe and gain the same level of performance as competitors complete exhaust packages.

mods.impact_note: This transforms a Gen 4 sled, but read the conditions first: the maker's page showed the kit sold out when checked. Silber's distinctive approach is a proprietary reflash of the factory ECU — your ECU must be sent in for it — after which the maker claims no further tuning is needed whatever boost or elevation you run, with boost adjustable in the 3–10 psi range. No clutch kit or clutching components are included and the standard kit ships without an intercooler, so the headline price is not the whole spend; a turbocharged engine also ends any realistic factory warranty expectation and lives or dies by boost and fuel discipline.

The gain shows up in deep snow and on climbs, where quick backshifting keeps track speed up under load, and the magnetic weights let you fine-tune without a full teardown. It is bolt-in and reversible, though a clutch puller and spring compressor make the job easier — and the maker's page showed it sold out when checked.

The maker claims 190 hp on pump gas and 200 hp on 110 octane; the second figure comes with a race-fuel routine, and both are maker claims, not verified numbers. Unless you buy outright you must send in your cylinders, exhaust valves and head, so the sled is down while that happens, and a modified engine like this ends any realistic expectation of factory engine warranty coverage.

Powder Lite cans are the loud end of the range, so the real cost is noise and exposure where mufflers are checked or trails are shared. It suits riders cutting front-end weight for mountain riding, not riders on groomed trails near homes.

That makes it a tuning tool for riders who change elevation or have added power elsewhere and need to correct rpm, not a performance gain by itself. You must pick the right elevation calibration at order, 0–3000' or 3000'+, because that calibration is part of the kit. It suits riders who want weight off and a crisper sound without committing to a full pipe set.

mods.product_name: Ski-Doo 850 G4/G5: Stage 2

The elevation choice at order is not a formality: you must select the 0–3000' or 3000'+ calibration, and picking the wrong one gives back much of the gain. It suits riders who want a complete, matched package instead of piecing exhaust and clutching together themselves.

Straightline recommends adding adjustable pDrive weights to help enhance the power, which is an honest signal that clutching may be needed to use whatever gain is there. On its own the change is modest — it makes most sense as part of a matched exhaust package.

No fuel changes are required, but Straightline warns clutching may need an adjustable weight kit depending on application, so budget for that possibility. It is a middle path: more than a can, less than a full pipe set, priced and performing accordingly.

mods.product_name: Ski-doo Rev Gen 4 & 5 / Lynx Radien 850 E-TEC 129-137″ Track Performance Trail Kit (0-3000ft) Clutch Kit
mods.fitment_statement: Ski-doo Rev Gen 4 & 5 / Lynx Radien 850 E-TEC 129-137″ and 146″ trail ridden Machines Performance Trail Kit 0-3000ft (part #121-238 per the maker Y-pipe instruction sheet). Mapped to 129/137 records of all lines and to 146 trail/crossover lines (Backcountry, Xterrain).
claims: Straightline Performances clutch kits are designed to give excellent hole shot, improved mid-range and best possible mph available. Clutch kits are dyno and field tested!

mods.impact_note: This kit adds no power — it recalibrates the clutches for low-elevation trail sleds on 129–137-inch tracks, and the maker claims excellent hole shot, improved mid-range and the best possible mph, with dyno and field testing behind it. Those are maker claims with no numbers attached, and the calibration is specific to 0–3000 ft, so it is the wrong kit for mountain elevations. It suits trail riders who feel the stock calibration leaves response on the table at the elevations they actually ride.

That certification is the reason to pick it over the louder options if your trails enforce sound rules, though certification on paper is not a guarantee in every jurisdiction. No clutching or fuel changes are required, and the honest expectation is weight off, not power on.

The maker rates the sound level as Race/Mountain, which means loud, and that makes it a backcountry part rather than a trail part where muffler rules apply. No clutching or fuel changes are required, so install is simple and the noise is the whole trade-off.

No fuel or clutching changes are needed, so install is simple, but that under-load noise makes it a backcountry part, not a trail part — some trail systems and jurisdictions restrict aftermarket mufflers. The maker's page showed this Gen 4 version currently out of stock when checked.

No fuel or clutching changes are needed, and the maker guarantees performance as good as or better than stock — a maker claim, as with every can here. It is the GGB most defensible on a trail sled, though local muffler rules can still apply.

mods.product_name: GGB Quiet Muffler — Ski-Doo Gen 4 850 E-TEC

That restraint makes it the MBRP most defensible on noise-sensitive trails, though aftermarket-muffler rules can still apply. It does not fit wide-body models: Expedition, Grand Touring, Enduro and Skandic are excluded.

mods.product_name: Ski-Doo (Lynx) G4 850 Turbo Kit 2017-2022
mods.fitment_statement: Product title (maker-stated at generation + years level; no individual models named): Ski-Doo (Lynx) G4 850 Turbo Kit 2017-2022. Maker lists the kit from $3,250.00 USD depending on variant; headline price $3,750.00 USD. Shown as Sold out on the maker page at check date.
claims: We are the first company to utilize the factory ECU/ECM to control fueling requirements for the turbo. This means no tuning no matter what boost you run or what elevation you run at.
Boost levels adjustable by the user between 3-10psi; with wastegate actuator springs, control your boost from 3-12psi. Silber notes the kit comes preset with a 7psi spring.
This kit is the easiest turbo to install on the market with no cutting, welding or drilling required.

Standard kit ships without intercooler.
No clutch kit or clutching components are listed as included.
mods.impact_note: This transforms a Gen 4 sled, but read the conditions first: the maker's page showed the kit sold out when checked. Silber's distinctive approach is a proprietary reflash of the factory ECU — your ECU must be sent in for it — after which the maker claims no further tuning is needed whatever boost or elevation you run, with boost adjustable in the 3–10 psi range. No clutch kit or clutching components are included and the standard kit ships without an intercooler, so the headline price is not the whole spend; a turbocharged engine also ends any realistic factory warranty expectation and lives or dies by boost and fuel discipline.

Speedwerx states it is designed for competition use only and suggests closed-course racing only — take that seriously: this is not a trail muffler, and noise rules are the obvious problem anywhere else. mods.product_name: Ski-Doo Etec 850 N.A Stage 2 Clutch Kit

Increased Top-End Track Speed

mods.impact_note: Adds no power — it changes how the power you have reaches the snow, and the maker claims faster backshifting, increased top-end track speed and improved throttle response. The gain shows up in deep snow and on climbs, where quick backshifting keeps track speed up under load, and the magnetic weights let you fine-tune without a full teardown. It is bolt-in and reversible, though a clutch puller and spring compressor make the job easier — and the maker's page showed it sold out when checked.

mods.product_name: Performance Big Bore Ultimate Kit / Skidoo 911

mods.impact_note: This is a system, not a bolt-on — cylinders, pistons, pipe, y-pipe, fuel module and a Stage 2 clutch kit are all in the box, because a bigger engine on stock exhaust and clutching would waste the displacement. The maker claims 190 hp on pump gas and 200 hp on 110 octane; the second figure comes with a race-fuel routine, and both are maker claims, not verified numbers. Unless you buy outright you must send in your cylinders, exhaust valves and head, so the sled is down while that happens, and a modified engine like this ends any realistic expectation of factory engine warranty coverage.

mods.product_name: '17-22 E-TEC 850 FULL VELOCITY MUFFLER - BLACK

Expect a louder, freer-flowing can and whatever front-end weight comes off with the stock muffler, with noise the main thing other riders will notice. Some trail systems and jurisdictions restrict aftermarket mufflers, so it suits mountain and off-trail use better than noise-sensitive trails.

mods.impact_note: The maker claims this muffler weighs a mere 5 lb and sheds 10 lb of factory weight off the front end — as with most cans, that weight saving and a much louder note are the real purchase, not a verified power gain. It is a race/mountain-style can, so it will be substantially louder than stock and a poor fit where trail muffler rules are enforced. It suits mountain riders chasing front-end weight savings who ride away from noise enforcement.

mods.impact_note: The maker claims this can weighs only 5 lb and loses 10 lb from the sled, and bills it as a race/mountain exhaust — weight and sound are what you are actually buying, not a verified power gain. Powder Lite cans are the loud end of the range, so the real cost is noise and exposure where mufflers are checked or trails are shared. It suits riders cutting front-end weight for mountain riding, not riders on groomed trails near homes.

delivering a proven 4 to 5 horsepower gain and noticeably stronger torque across the entire RPM range

Bikeman says no ECU tune is required to run it standalone, which makes it a low-commitment bolt-on. On its own the change is modest — it makes most sense as part of a matched exhaust package rather than as a standalone power buy.

mods.product_name: pDrive Adjustable Weight Pivot Bolt Kit (12–20.6g) for Ski-Doo 850 E-TEC
mods.fitment_statement: Primary Application: 2017+ Ski-Doo REV Gen4 & Gen5 850 E-TEC snowmobiles (Summit, Freeride, Renegade, MXZ, and Backcountry models).

That makes it a tuning tool for riders who change elevation or have added power elsewhere and need to correct rpm, not a performance gain by itself. Installation needs clean threads, threadlocker and torque to factory pDrive specifications, so it rewards careful work.

mods.product_name: Ski-Doo 850 Stage 1
mods.fitment_statement: Product options: 2017-18 / 2019-20 / 2021-22 / 2023-27 850 MXZ, 850 Renegade and 850 Summit (model options verbatim in research notes).

requirements: Elevation calibration must be selected at order: 0-3000' or 3000'+.
mods.impact_note: Stage 1 is the lighter step: a silencer and Powder Valve intake kit, with a Power Shift clutch kit included on some models, and the maker claims 7.1 lb saved and 'a couple extra horsepower' — a deliberately modest claim. You must pick the right elevation calibration at order, 0–3000' or 3000'+, because that calibration is part of the kit. It suits riders who want weight off and a crisper sound without committing to a full pipe set.

mods.product_name: Ski-Doo 850 G4/G5: Stage 2
mods.fitment_statement: Product options: 2017-18 / 2019-20 / 2021-22 / 2023-27 850 MXZ, 850 Renegade and 850 Summit (model options verbatim in research notes).
claims: Delivering an additional 7.3 horsepower and 4.9 ft/lbs of torque while trimming 10.1 pounds of weight
An arm stretching 6 lengths quicker than stock in a 1/4 mile drag race is what you will see in the field.
requirements: Elevation calibration must be selected at order: 0-3000' or 3000'+.
Kit includes a Single Pipe Set (y-pipe, pipe and silencer), Powder Valve Intake Kit and a Power Shift Clutch Kit.
mods.impact_note: The classic naturally aspirated recipe — a matched single pipe set, intake and clutch kit tuned to work together, which is why the maker's claim is modest and specific: an additional 7.3 horsepower and 4.9 ft-lb of torque while trimming 10.1 lb. The elevation choice at order is not a formality: you must select the 0–3000' or 3000'+ calibration, and picking the wrong one gives back much of the gain. It suits riders who want a complete, matched package instead of piecing exhaust and clutching together themselves.

mods.product_name: 2017-27 850 Ski-Doo Single Pipe Sets

claims: Increased horsepower and lighter weight; two things SLP exhaust systems are well known for.
mods.impact_note: This is a full pipe set, the part of the exhaust where a naturally aspirated engine can actually gain — but SLP prints no numeric power or weight figure for it, only a general claim of increased horsepower and lighter weight, so there is no number to hold it to. The kits include detailed instructions covering clutching and EFI mapping information, which tells you setup matters if you want whatever gain is there. The G4 trail fitment expressly excludes the 2017 Renegade Backcountry, so check the exact variant for your sled.

mods.product_name: 2017-27 850 Ski-Doo G4 & G5 REV Lightweight Silencer

SLP tested and passed SAE J-2567 stationary sound test below 88 decibels.

No ECU modification is required, and SLP notes it is compatible with its single pipe, so a pipe can be added later. In the real world this is weight off the sled and a different note, not a power increase — the sensible buy if you may build toward a pipe later.

mods.product_name: Comp. Series Silencer for Ski-Doo 850 G4/G5 Models

That makes it a weight-first can for riders who accept more noise at full throttle. The fitment variants captured from the maker are Gen 4 only, despite the G4/G5 product title, so Gen 5 riders should not assume coverage.

mods.product_name: Clutch Kits - Ski-Doo (Power Shift Clutch Kits)
mods.fitment_statement: Product options: 850 E-TEC 2017-21 MXZ, 850 E-TEC 2017-27 Renegade, 850 E-TEC 2017-27 Summit
claims: Get your horsepower to the ground with SLP Power Shift Clutch Kits!
On short track models, these kits deliver instantaneous throttle response with wicked acceleration.
requirements: Buyer must select model, exhaust configuration (Stock/Silencer, Stock/Stage 1, Stage 1, SLP Single Pipe, Stage 2, Stage 3) and elevation band. Price shown is the maker page starting price for the multi-application page; 850 variant prices are not separated on the page.
mods.impact_note: This adds no power — it is about getting the power you have to the snow, and SLP claims its Magnum Force weights improve belt pinch, acceleration and belt slippage. You must order it matched to your model, your exhaust configuration and your elevation band; a kit ordered for the wrong exhaust or elevation misses the point entirely. Note the price carried in this data is the maker page's starting price for a multi-application page, not a separated 850 price, so confirm the actual variant price before relying on it.

mods.product_name: Ski-Doo 850 REV Gen 4, Gen 5 & Lynx Radian High-Performance Y-Pipe
mods.fitment_statement: Product title: Ski-Doo 850 REV Gen 4, Gen 5 & Lynx Radian High-Performance Y-Pipe (ceramic coated 134-174; high-temp black 134-175 per the maker instruction sheets). Price range by coating option: $249.95 to $274.95 USD.

There are no fuel programming changes required to run the Straightline 850 E-TEC Ypipe.
requirements: Straightline recommends adding an Adjustable P-Drive Weights to your snowmobile to help enhance the power.
mods.impact_note: A y-pipe is a supporting piece, not a full exhaust: the maker claims a proven 5+ horsepower gain, which is a maker claim, and says no fuel programming changes are required to run it. Straightline recommends adding adjustable pDrive weights to help enhance the power, which is an honest signal that clutching may be needed to use whatever gain is there. On its own the change is modest — it makes most sense as part of a matched exhaust package.

mods.product_name: Skidoo 850 Rev Gen 4 / Lynx Radien High Performance Exhaust – Combo Ceramic Coated (Includes 134-173, 134-174)
mods.fitment_statement: Maker fitment table: Ski-Doo 850 E-TEC Backcountry, MXZ, Renegade, Summit for 2017–2022 plus 2023 Backcountry rows, and Lynx 850 E-TEC (RAIDEN) rows. Does not include a single pipe. (Maker table also prints 2025–2026 rows; not applied — the product is the maker-named Rev Gen 4 combo. See research notes.)
claims: HP Gain | 5 HP
Weight loss | 7.5 lbs
A Complete Performance Exhaust package at a fraction of the price, use your stock single pipe and gain the same level of performance as competitors complete exhaust packages.

mods.impact_note: This combo pairs Straightline's y-pipe with its lightweight muffler and keeps your stock single pipe, and the maker claims 5 horsepower and a 7.5 lb weight loss for the package — maker claims, with the muffler half of it elsewhere rated by the same maker as matching stock on power. No fuel changes are required, but Straightline warns clutching may need an adjustable weight kit depending on application, so budget for that possibility. It is a middle path: more than a can, less than a full pipe set, priced and performing accordingly.

mods.product_name: Ski-doo Rev Gen 4 & 5 / Lynx Radien 850 E-TEC 129-137″ Track Performance Trail Kit (0-3000ft) Clutch Kit
mods.fitment_statement: Ski-doo Rev Gen 4 & 5 / Lynx Radien 850 E-TEC 129-137″ and 146″ trail ridden Machines Performance Trail Kit 0-3000ft (part #121-238 per the maker Y-pipe instruction sheet). Mapped to 129/137 records of all lines and to 146 trail/crossover lines (Backcountry, Xterrain).
claims: Straightline Performances clutch kits are designed to give excellent hole shot, improved mid-range and best possible mph available. Clutch kits are dyno and field tested!
requirements: Elevation-specific: 0-3000ft calibration.
mods.impact_note: This kit adds no power — it recalibrates the clutches for low-elevation trail sleds on 129–137-inch tracks, and the maker claims excellent hole shot, improved mid-range and the best possible mph, with dyno and field testing behind it. Those are maker claims with no numbers attached, and the calibration is specific to 0–3000 ft, so it is the wrong kit for mountain elevations. It suits trail riders who feel the stock calibration leaves response on the table at the elevations they actually ride.

mods.product_name: Ski-doo 850 Rev Gen 4 / Lynx Radien Lightweight Muffler Ceramic Coated
mods.fitment_statement: Maker fitment table: Ski-Doo 850 E-TEC Backcountry, MXZ, Renegade, Summit (2017–2022 rows captured). Maker table is internally inconsistent (Gen 4 name with later-year rows); mapped to the Gen4-era rows only — see research notes.

mods.impact_note: The measured option in Straightline's Gen 4 range: the maker claims a 7.5 lb weight loss and horsepower that matches stock, and states the muffler is SAE J192, J1161 and SAE 2567 certified. That certification is the reason to pick it over the louder options if your trails enforce sound rules, though certification on paper is not a guarantee in every jurisdiction. No clutching or fuel changes are required, and the honest expectation is weight off, not power on.

mods.product_name: Ski-doo 850 Rev Gen 4 / Lynx Radien Ultra Lite Muffler Polished Stainless Steel

The maker rates the sound level as Race/Mountain, which means loud, and that makes it a backcountry part rather than a trail part where muffler rules apply. No clutching or fuel changes are required, so install is simple and the noise is the whole trade-off.

mods.product_name: Ski-doo 850 Rev Gen 4 / Lynx Radien Carbon Fiber Muffler Stainless Steel

The maker rates its sound level as Race/Mountain, which means loud, with the trail-legality problems that follow anywhere mufflers are checked. No clutching or fuel changes are required, so the trade is simple: a lot of weight for a lot of noise, at a carbon-fibre price.

mods.product_name: GGB Mountain Muffler — Ski-Doo Gen 4 850 E-TEC

mods.impact_note: This is a weight-and-sound mod, not a power mod: the maker claims 10.65 lb saved and prints the noise honestly, +4–6 dBA at idle and +10–18 dBA under load. No fuel or clutching changes are needed, so install is simple, but that under-load noise makes it a backcountry part, not a trail part — some trail systems and jurisdictions restrict aftermarket mufflers. The maker's page showed this Gen 4 version currently out of stock when checked.

No fuel or clutching changes are needed, and the maker guarantees performance as good as or better than stock — a maker claim, as with every can here. It is the GGB most defensible on a trail sled, though local muffler rules can still apply.

mods.product_name: GGB Quiet Muffler — Ski-Doo Gen 4 850 E-TEC
mods.fitment_statement: GGB's per-year/per-model fitment list for this part number (ggbexhaust.com, checked 2026-11-21), summarised by the maker's own short-form list: 2017-2022 Gen 4 850 E-TEC MXZ/Renegade/Summit/Backcountry/Freeride, plus 2023 Gen 4 Backcountry / Backcountry X / Backcountry XRS; the same list names Lynx Boondocker DS, Rave RE and Xterrain RE entries for 2022–2023 (full list in research notes). mods.impact_note: The Quiet is the restrained end of GGB's range: the maker claims 6.75 lb saved and dyno-tested performance as good as or better than stock, for riders who want a deeper note and the weight saving without the Mountain muffler's noise penalty. mods.product_name: Race Series Snowmobile Exhaust, 1320309

In practice this is a sound-first can for riders who accept the noise — the wrong pick for groomed trails, populated areas or anywhere mufflers are checked. It does not fit wide-body models: Expedition, Grand Touring, Enduro and Skandic are excluded.

That makes it a reasonable trail choice where a can is allowed at all. It does not fit wide-body models: Expedition, Grand Touring, Enduro and Skandic are excluded.

mods.product_name: Quiet Series Snowmobile Exhaust, 132Q106

That restraint makes it the MBRP most defensible on noise-sensitive trails, though aftermarket-muffler rules can still apply. It does not fit wide-body models: Expedition, Grand Touring, Enduro and Skandic are excluded.

mods.product_name: Ski-Doo (Lynx) G4 850 Turbo Kit 2017-2022
mods.fitment_statement: Product title (maker-stated at generation + years level; no individual models named): Ski-Doo (Lynx) G4 850 Turbo Kit 2017-2022. Maker lists the kit from $3,250.00 USD depending on variant; headline price $3,750.00 USD. Shown as Sold out on the maker page at check date.
claims: We are the first company to utilize the factory ECU/ECM to control fueling requirements for the turbo. This means no tuning no matter what boost you run or what elevation you run at.
Boost levels adjustable by the user between 3-10psi; with wastegate actuator springs, control your boost from 3-12psi. Silber notes the kit comes preset with a 7psi spring.
This kit is the easiest turbo to install on the market with no cutting, welding or drilling required.
requirements: ECU must be sent in for Silber's proprietary reflash: "Do I need to send back my ECU for a reflash? Yes you need to send us your ECU if you purchase a kit."
Standard kit ships without intercooler.
No clutch kit or clutching components are listed as included.
mods.impact_note: This transforms a Gen 4 sled, but read the conditions first: the maker's page showed the kit sold out when checked. Silber's distinctive approach is a proprietary reflash of the factory ECU — your ECU must be sent in for it — after which the maker claims no further tuning is needed whatever boost or elevation you run, with boost adjustable in the 3–10 psi range. No clutch kit or clutching components are included and the standard kit ships without an intercooler, so the headline price is not the whole spend; a turbocharged engine also ends any realistic factory warranty expectation and lives or dies by boost and fuel discipline.

Speedwerx says its mufflers perform the same or better than stock, use the stock outlet location and need no chassis modifications. Expect weight and a modest sound increase, not a power gain.

mods.product_name: L2 Competition Series Lightweight Muffler // Ceramic Coated // 2017-2023 Ski-Doo Gen 4 600R / 850 Summit/Renegade/MXZ
